text: What makes boson sampling a credible demonstration that quantum dynamics outruns classical simulation?
choices: It is a universal, error-corrected quantum computer
Its output amplitudes are permanents of submatrices, and the permanent is #P-hard, so efficient classical sampling would collapse the polynomial hierarchy
Its amplitudes are determinants, which are exponentially hard to compute
It can factor large integers faster than Shor's algorithm
explanation: Boson-sampling amplitudes are matrix permanents, which are #P-hard (Valiant, 1979); Aaronson and Arkhipov (2011) showed efficient classical sampling would collapse the polynomial hierarchy. It is explicitly NOT universal or error-corrected (choice 0); determinants (fermionic scattering) are easy, O(n^3) (choice 2); and it does not run Shor/factoring (choice 3).
